title: Check Array Formation Through Concatenation
statement:
You have an array `arr` of distinct integers and a list `pieces` of integer arrays; no integer appears twice anywhere in `pieces`. You may lay the arrays of `pieces` end to end in any order you like, but the numbers inside each piece must keep their own order.

Return `true` if some order of the pieces joins into exactly `arr`, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: The integers in arr are distinct
All integers across pieces are distinct (after flattening pieces)
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every order of the pieces is factorial work. The distinct values remove all choice: whatever number sits at the current position of `arr` can be the first number of at most one piece, so that piece is forced. Index the pieces by their first number in a hash map, then walk `arr` once and check that each forced piece matches the stretch of `arr` it must cover.

## Approach

1. Build `pieceByFirst`, mapping each piece's first value to the piece.
2. Start `i` at 0. While `i` is inside `arr`, look up the piece that starts with `arr[i]`.
3. If there is none, `arr[i]` cannot be placed: return `false`.
4. Otherwise compare the piece with `arr` value by value, advancing `i`; any difference means `false`.
5. If the walk reaches the end of `arr`, every position was covered in order: return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [15, 88]`, `pieces = [[88], [15]]`, so `pieceByFirst` is `{88 → [88], 15 → [15]}`.

- `i = 0`: `arr[0] = 15` finds `[15]`; it matches and `i` becomes 1.
- `i = 1`: `arr[1] = 88` finds `[88]`; it matches and `i` becomes 2.
- `i` has reached the end, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): the map takes one step per piece and the walk visits each position of `arr` once.
- Space: O(m) for the map, where m is the number of pieces.

## Pitfalls

- Matching only first values is not enough; every value of the piece must line up (Example 2 fails on order).
- A piece may contain a number that is not in `arr`; the value-by-value comparison catches it.
- Advance `i` inside the inner loop, so the next lookup starts right after the piece just used.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pieceByFirst` | first value of a piece → that piece |
| `i` | the next position of `arr` still to be covered |
| `piece` | the piece forced to start at position `i` |
| `value` | the piece's value being compared with `arr[i]` |

narration.2: Index every piece by its first value; distinct values make each key unique.
narration.3: Go through the pieces once to fill the map.
narration.7: i is the first position of arr that no piece covers yet.
narration.8: Keep placing pieces until all of arr is covered.
narration.9: Only the piece starting with arr[i] can go here.
narration.10: No piece starts with this value, so arr cannot be formed.
narration.13: Walk through the chosen piece in its fixed order.
narration.14: Each value of the piece must equal the matching value of arr.
narration.17: Move to the next position of arr.
narration.20: Every position was covered in order, so arr can be formed.
